steps.scene: You're in a queue at a busy junction. At the last moment you realise you're in the wrong lane for where you want to go.

options.text: Cut into the correct lane while there's still a gap
Carry on in the lane you're in and find another way round
Stop and wait for someone to let you across

question.explanation: A last-moment lane change is how side-swipes happen. Go where your lane takes you: it costs you a minute.

steps.title: The right-hand lane
steps.body: On a dual carriageway the right-hand lane is for overtaking or turning right. Move back to the left once you're past.

question.prompt: When should you use the right-hand lane of a three-lane dual carriageway?

options.text: When you're overtaking or turning right
Whenever you want to travel faster than the traffic on your left
As soon as the road widens to three lanes

question.explanation: There's no 'fast lane'. The right-hand lane is for overtaking or turning right — the left-hand lane is where you belong.

steps.title: One-way streets
steps.body: In a one-way street every vehicle is going the same way, so you may pass on the right or on the left.

question.prompt: Where may you overtake on a one-way street?

options.text: On either the right or the left
On the right only, as on any other road
Nowhere — overtaking is banned in one-way streets

question.explanation: Nothing is coming the other way, so either side is legal. Pick the lane your exit needs, early, and stay in it.

a.label: Solid white line
a.body: The cycle lane is in operation. You must not drive or park in it during its hours.

b.label: Broken white line
b.body: Advisory: keep out unless it's unavoidable, and never park in it.

question.prompt: A cycle lane beside you is marked with a solid white line. What does that mean for you?

options.text: You must not drive or park in it
You may use it while the traffic beside it is slow
It's advice only, so you may drive in it

question.explanation: A solid line makes it compulsory: that strip of road isn't yours while the lane is operating.

steps.title: Bus lanes
steps.body: The sign at the start of a bus lane shows who may use it and when. Outside those times, other traffic may use it too.

question.prompt: When may you drive a car in a bus lane?

options.text: Outside its hours of operation, as shown on the sign
Whenever there's no bus in sight
Never, at any time of day

question.explanation: Read the plate. Some bus lanes run only at peak times, some run all day. Empty is not the same as allowed.

steps.scene: You're on a main road, about to turn left into a side road. There's a cyclist somewhere behind you.

question.prompt: How should you position the car on the approach?

options.text: Keep well to the left, so nobody can come up your inside
Move out to the middle so you can swing in wide
Straddle both lanes so drivers know you're slowing

question.explanation: Keeping left closes the gap a cyclist or moped could ride into, and it shows everyone behind exactly what you're doing.

steps.wrongBelief: Putting your indicator on gives you the right to move into the next lane.

options.text: It's right — a signal makes the space yours
A signal is only information — you still have to find a safe gap
Signals aren't needed when you change lane

question.explanation: Mirror, signal, manoeuvre — in that order. Nobody has to make room for you because your indicator is on.

steps.repairNote: A signal says what you intend. Check the mirror and the blind spot, and move only when the gap is really there.
